name: Base 46 vs Pro I-Form
formation: 46 Front vs Pro I-Form Strong Right
frontName: 46 Front (Head-Up Ends, Bunched LBs, Walked Safeties)

summary.motive: Commit nine defenders to the box with walked safeties and bunched linebackers so any base run is met at or behind the line of scrimmage with a blocker-free defender.
summary.keyDefender: SS at 5 yards — the extra force player who turns every one-gap run into a two-hat fit
summary.whyItWorks: Offensive blocking rules cannot account for both walked safeties; the FB kick meets a squeezing end instead of a linebacker, and the ball carrier runs into a pre-built pile.
summary.failureMode: Any completion beats zero coverage: with no deep safety, a double move or quick slant against isolated press corners is a touchdown threat.

beats.title: 1. The Eight-Man Box Picture
beats.text: Both safeties are walked into the box at 5 and 8 yards with all three linebackers bunched at 2.5 yards. There is no deep-middle defender anywhere — the offense sees nine hats within 6 yards of the ball.

beats.title: 2. Head-Up Ends Refuse to Be Reached
beats.text: The 46 ends align head-up rather than shaded, so neither tackle nor the tight end can reach an outside shoulder. Both ends strike and squeeze, spilling any kick-out back into the bunched linebackers.

beats.title: 3. NOSE Splits, Linebackers Scrape
beats.text: The 0-tech nose absorbs the center-guard double team and splits it toward the ball, while MIKE rips over the guard climb and SAM scrapes behind the squeezing end. Every gap has two defenders.

beats.title: 4. Ten Hats at the Football
beats.text: The running back is met at the line by MIKE with SS and FS stacking in behind. The run never touches the second level — the defining picture of Buddy Ryan’s 46.

relations.tell: Both safeties aligned INSIDE the tackles at 5 and 8 yards — the pure 46 picture has no safety deeper than the linebackers’ original depth.
